answers.In a sentence or two, what will it do fo: It approves or declines personal loan applications by itself and sends the decision straight to the customer, with no human review.
What information will it see or use? Tic: Information about people — clients, applicants, staff or anyone else: names, contact details, account and financial details, CVs — anything about someone who can be identified
answers.What happens with what it produces? If i: acts entirely by itself, with no person involved at any point
answers.What does it do when it acts?: Makes a yes-or-no decision — e.g. accepts or declines an application, signs something off
answers.Who ends up seeing or receiving what it: Clients or customers — including people applying to us
answers.Which of these does it help decide, if a: Whether to lend to someone, or on what terms
answers.How widely will it be used?: My team, as part of normal work

expectNext: After Continue, I expect to go to step 4, Questions, which may ask a few more things. Then step 5, Confirm, to check my answers. Then step 6, Result, which tells me whether we can go ahead and what needs doing first. The tool will have been checked against the firm's written rules, not decided by AI. I don't know what step 2, Similar checks, does or where it fits. I also expect to be able to change my answers before anything is decided.
ticksMean: "I've checked this answer" means I have read the helper's suggested answer for that question and agree it is right. Until I tick it, or change the answer, it doesn't count and I can't continue. So the tick is my confirmation, and the answer becomes mine, not the helper's. It does not mean the tool is approved. The ✓ and ○ marks in "What your description mentions" are different. They only show whether my words touched a topic, not whether I answered it or whether it is right.
comment: As a hurried relationship manager, I ticked all three pre-fills because they matched my description. I answered Not sure to the rest of the questions I couldn't answer from the packet, such as supplier, kind of AI, whether it replaces something, and whether mistakes can be put right. I also ticked "Somewhere else, or not sure" for countries, because the packet doesn't say where I work.
